transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-01
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 50 minutes
Attendees: Lena Martinez (Redwood AE), Amit Patel (Redwood SE), Chris Wong (Redwood SRE), Jordan Lee (CTO, Boreal Harvest), Priya Raman (ML Eng), Marcus Hale (Infra), Elena Soto (PM)

Summary: quick sync on POC latency results, new microburst anomalies, discussion of sequence length tradeoffs, kernel selection options, and next steps for SSO + security docs. Agreement to run longer microburst test and schedule kernel-level deep dive.

Topics: TTFT (time-to-first-token), streaming-first-response, sequence length distributions, kernel choices, prefix/KV cache behavior, quantization tradeoffs, SOC2/KMS questions

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: hi everybody thanks for joining, we'll kick off — quick agenda, run through last week's numbers, microburst anomalies, kernel choices, and actions. Amit you wanna start with the numbers?
[00:27] Amit: yeah sure, lemme share the dashboard, uh the short story: running the hosted variant on our test cluster we saw median TTFT around 45ms for seq‑len 256, but microburst events spiked to 650ms a handful of times during the 4 hour run.
[00:48] Jordan: 650 is...yeah that's higher than we expected. Are those the ones at the same time each day?
[00:55] Amit: not exactly, looks correlated with small concurrent bursts — multiple short chat completions at once. The KV cache hit rate was about 28% for these traces which is lower than expected since our prompts aren't identical.
[01:20] Priya: quick q — are we using prefix caching or full kv caching? I thought we enabled prefix but the logs were ambiguous.
[01:28] Amit: we enabled prefix caching only, but there were a couple edge cases where the cache TTL dropped because of sequence mismatch, so effective hits were lower.
[01:42] Marcus: can you explain the sequence mismatch bit? we do have variable prompt lengths across product calls.
[01:50] Amit: yeah so some calls have debug headers and dynamic metadata — the prefix doesn't match exactly, so the KV key changes. We're proposing a normalized prefix preproc to boost hit rate.
[02:10] Lena: okay that dovetails with the suggestion from last week to try len bucketing. Amit, did you test batching with bucketing turned on?
[02:22] Amit: preliminary, yes. With bucketing we saw median TTFT up 8ms because of small batching delay but tail improved — the 95th percentile dropped from 220ms to 160ms for seq_len 256. But for seq_len 1024 batching overhead is different, and kernel selection matters.
[02:48] Jordan: kernel selection — can you explain that again? I remember you mentioned two kernel families.
[02:55] Amit: yeah, roughly the "stream-optimized" kernel gives faster initial token generation (better TTFT) but it's suboptimal for long sequences because it has more memory churn. The "fused-matmul" kernel is heavier for first token but better amortized for long seq. There's also a newer quant-friendly kernel that helps 4-bit runs.
[03:20] Elena: question — from product POV we mostly need fast first response for search suggestions, so TTFT is king. But we also have some longer completions for summarization. How do we pick?
[03:33] Lena: that's the tradeoff — you pick routing rules: short requests go to stream-optimized, long requests go to fused. Redwood can do automatic routing by seq_len, or you can pin by endpoint.
[03:46] Marcus: are these routing rules in the private deploy too? we will probably move to private VPC later.
[03:52] Chris (SRE): yes, same runtime supports private but you need to map the policies — there is a config flag in the control plane. NOTE: SRE attribution may be wrong in transcript.
[04:05] Jordan: ok we're planning private next quarter but for now pilot is hosted. security is still important — whats the plan for KMS and logs?
[04:15] Lena: we'll share security pack — SOC2 cert, KMS integration diagram, and audit-log retention options. We can integrate with your KMS or use Redwood-managed keys.
[04:29] Priya: if you use redwood keys do we have beta key export? we've got compliance constraints.
[04:36] Lena: Redwood-managed keys are typical but for Boreal we'd recommend customer-managed KMS, we have an HSM integration flow. We'll include that doc.
[04:48] Marcus: thanks. Back to microburst — any hypothesis on why it's spiky rather than steady?
[04:55] Amit: couple hypotheses: 1) scheduling jitter when GPUs shift batches between kernels; 2) sudden cache churn due to metadata changing; 3) quantization fallback causing kernel switch. We saw one event that looked like a kernel swap mid-request.
[05:12] Priya: kernel swap mid-request — is that safe? wouldn't that cause correctness issues?
[05:18] Amit: it's designed to be safe: we checkpoint the KV and restart on compatible kernel, but it does add latency. We can avoid mid-request switches by pre-probing sequence length and assigning kernel upfront.
[05:32] Jordan: aha so if we pre-probe we avoid the swap latency but add a small scheduling step. Is that included in your routing?
[05:40] Amit: we can do pre-probe in the first 2ms by inspecting the payload length; it's fast and worth it for tail savings.
[05:48] Lena: Lena interrupts: also consider queuing policy — small priority queue for interactive calls to reduce head-of-line blocking.
[05:56] Elena: that might help our search latency. Any cost impact?
[06:02] Amit: priority queues increase throughput variance, but cost delta is small; it's more an ops/config play.
[06:09] Jordan: can you show the 24h microburst run numbers?
[06:13] Amit: I have a short excerpt: over 24h we saw 20 microburst spikes (above 500ms) mostly during CI window and morning traffic and a few random ones.
[06:25] Marcus: CI window — do you mean our nightly scraping? could be unrelated. We'll check.
[06:29] Jordan: action: Marcus to correlate internal cron jobs with spikes.
[06:33] Marcus: noted.
[06:35] [07:00] Amit: switching to quantization — we ran 4-bit quant (RWQ) on a sample model and saw nominal CPU/GPU throughput improvements; TTFT improved a bit but tail increased slightly due to dequant overhead on first token.
[07:21] Priya: so quant helps cost but could worsen TTFT tail? that's tricky.
[07:27] Amit: yes exact tradeoff. For short responses quant gains are marginal because overhead dominates. For long generation it's worth it.
[07:35] Lena: so strategy might be: keep non-quantized for short interactive endpoints, enable quant for long offline batch jobs and low-priority endpoints.
[07:46] Elena: what's the config complexity? can we flip per-route?
[07:50] Chris: yes per-route config and we support canary rollouts for quant profiles.
[07:57] [10:00] Jordan: can we get a recommended config for our mix? roughly 60% short search, 30% mid summaries, 10% long transcripts.
[10:10] Amit: recommendation: stream-optimized kernel + prefix caching + priority queue for short; fused kernel or quant for long. Use len-bucketing at 128/256/1024 boundaries. We'll provide a config snapshot.
[10:28] Priya: please include assumed cost delta for each change.
[10:32] Lena: will do; we'll put a cost model in the result doc.
[10:36] Marcus: one more infra note — do we need custom NIC settings for burst stability? some cloud VMs show jitter.
[10:44] Amit: high-performance NIC helps for multi-GPU sync; also kernel placement matters to avoid cross-socket stalls. We'll add infra tuning checklist.
[10:54] Jordan: regarding metrics — we need per-route token breakdown and token-level trace for a couple of sessions.
[11:02] Amit: we can provide token breakdown and per-token latencies; privacy note: traces will be redacted.
[11:08] Elena: on the rollout timeline — if we get microburst under control can we move to Dedicated in 6 weeks?
[11:14] Lena: that seems feasible, assuming the pilot stabilizes. Dedicated commit has lead time for capacity though.
[11:20] Jordan: ok put a target: stabilization within 6 weeks, decision meeting at end of that window.
[11:27] Lena: agreed.
[11:30] [20:00] Amit: experiment plan recap: 1) 24h microburst stress with seq_len 256 & 1024 and bucketing on/off. 2) Run quant vs non-quant smoke with TTFT sampling. 3) Kernel hedging test: pin kernel per-route vs pre-probe routing. We'll run each for 24h where feasible.
[20:28] Priya: can you also snapshot KV cache keys so we can see mismatch distribution?
[20:33] Amit: yes we'll capture sample keys and anonymize.
[20:39] Marcus: I'll try to correlate cron jobs and traffic schedule — I'll send logs.
[20:45] [30:00] Jordan: security follow-up — Lena send SOC2 + KMS diagram and also any penetration test reports.
[30:08] Lena: will do, I'll include retention options and the SAML SSO flow.
[30:14] Elena: we need SSO test accounts created; Jordan will handle.
[30:17] Jordan: ok.
[30:20] [35:00] Amit: small note on cost: enabling priority queue and stream kernel per-route increased baseline cost by approx 6% in our estimate but saves 30-40% tail latency incidents.
[35:14] Priya: that's acceptable if it improves UX.
[35:18] Lena: final blocker list: 1) microburst root cause (infra vs runtime) 2) SSO/KMS signoff 3) cost tradeoffs and quant profile decision
[35:30] Jordan: agree.
[35:34] [45:00] Lena: recap and next steps — Amit to run tests and share results by 2026-03-05; Lena to send security and pricing by 2026-03-03; Marcus to provide logs and correlate crons by 2026-03-06; schedule kernel deep-dive week of Mar 8. Anyone object?
[45:52] Marcus: no objections.
[46:00] Jordan: thanks everyone.
[46:05] Priya: thanks.
[46:08] Lena: thanks all, meeting adjourned.

References and links mentioned: "security pack (link)" (Lena to send), "24h microburst dashboard" (Amit will upload), "kernel deep-dive deck" (Amit/Lena to co-host).
